text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO breach detected for /v1/chat/stream (hosted). p99=3.82s (SLO=2.0s), p95=1.9s. Spike started ~2025-08-12T09:13Z. Affected cluster: us-west-2-serving-3. Impact ~2.1% of requests in last 10m. Pager: @alice

alice: I'm oncall — looking at grafana now. Can folks post any recent deploys to preproc/tokenizer or prompt template changes?

alice: quick snapshot from grafana (last 30m):
```
p50  0.42s
p95  1.94s
p99  3.82s
stream-gaps (median)  120ms  -> tail spikes 700-1200ms
queue_length preproc  avg 4.3 -> 12.8
cpu% preproc workers  85% -> 98%
requests/sec  ~2400 -> 1800 (errors rising)
```

bob: eng-ml here. We cut a tokenizer change at 09:05 that enabled "json-mode" validation for tool schemas (commit abc1234). It added stricter parsing + full-schema validation pre-send. I didn't expect CPU to go this high.

carla: runtime: seeing streaming stalls where the emitter pauses for ~800ms mid-response; downstream worker shows blocked syscalls. Not seeing KV cache pressure.

alice: hypothesis: preproc/tokenizer CPU blocking causes backpressure into runtime's streaming threads -> tail latency / stalls.

dave: SRE mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from us-west-2-serving-3 -> fallback pool 2) disable streaming for affected route 3) increase preproc replica count temporarily 4) revert tokenizer commit. Which do we want now?

alice: Do a quick mitigation list, in order: route small percentage initially then 100% if problem persists; disable streaming for verified customers; scale preproc; prepare revert. I'll coordinate.

carla: I can push a routing override now. Suggest: move 100% of requests tagged "json-mode" to m-medium-json (a smaller model with simpler preproc path) while we stabilize.

alice: applying routing override for json-mode requests to m-medium-json (temporary). Command:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/routes/override \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"selector":"meta.mode:json","target":"m-medium-json","weight":100}'
```

alice: route applied. monitoring...

eve: support: listing affected customers from logs (queries using json-mode): CUST-102, CUST-237, CUST-998. I'm drafting outbound msg to them.

bob: running a quick benchmark locally to confirm impact. Command: `python -m preproc.bench --json-mode --prompt-template=ui-schema-v2 --concurrency=8` -> result: avg preproc 420ms, p99 780ms. Without json-mode: avg 40ms. So big delta.

alice: thanks. That aligns. So root cause likely the new strict-schema validation in tokenizer. We should revert if safer.

dave: while revert is prepared, I'm scaling preproc pool +10 replicas (autoscaling policy bump). Doing that now.

carla: runtime notes: enabling streaming chunk fallback — will force smaller emission batches to reduce observed pauses. Patch pushed to canary.

alice: disable streaming selectively for those three affected customers to ensure their UX degrades gracefully (no stalls) instead of long pauses. Command to customer config:
```
PATCH /v1/customers/CUST-102/config {"streaming": false}
PATCH /v1/customers/CUST-237/config {"streaming": false}
PATCH /v1/customers/CUST-998/config {"streaming": false}
```

eve: outbound template to customers: "We're seeing intermittent streaming stalls for requests using advanced JSON tool schemas. We've temporarily disabled streaming for your account and routed requests to a stable path while we fix the tokenizer. No data exposure. Expected fix ETA 2-4 hours. We'll follow up." Sending now. :white_check_mark:

bob: reverting commit abc1234 in staging and preparing hotfix patch that keeps json-mode parsing but moves schema validation off the critical path into async validation (and adds a fast-path that skips full-schema for common templates). Hotfix branch: hotfix/tokenizer-json-async.

alice: great. Can we also add a short-term guard in the API to reject requests with huge schema bodies > 50KB? We're seeing a few customers send enormous tool schemas.

bob: yeah adding a size guard now: `if len(schema) > 50000: return 413` (soft-fail with explanatory message). I'll deploy to canary in 5m.

carla: canary of streaming chunk fallback looks promising — p99 on the canary pool dropped from 3.8s -> 1.6s.

alice: summary of mitigations executed (timestamps UTC):
- 09:16 applied route override for json-mode -> m-medium-json (carla)
- 09:18 scaled preproc +10 replicas (dave)
- 09:20 disabled streaming for CUST-102,237,998 (alice/eve)
- 09:22 deployed streaming-chunk fallback to canary (carla)
- 09:28 started revert/hotfix branch (bob)
- 09:35 added schema-size guard to canary (bob)

alice: customer impact: ~2.1% of requests impacted; 3 customers had streaming disabled as a precaution. No errors returned (mostly stalls/slow responses).

frank: from CS: notified CUST-102 (on call there) — they replied they're fine with fallback but want ETA. I'll ping when we have rollback plan.

bob: plan to ship hotfix to prod after quick smoke tests. Hotfix does: remove synchronous full-schema validation from the critical tokenizer path, run validation async and emit non-blocking warnings; keep smaller fast-path; add schema-size guard.

alice: can we get a deploy timeline?

bob: aim to merge in 30-45m and deploy staged 3-step (canary -> 10% -> 100%). If canary looks good we'll ramp.

gina: observability note: adding a short-lived metric "preproc.block_time_ms" and alert threshold p99>200ms so we catch regressions sooner. Pushing dashboard panel now.

alice: handoff to frank at 10:00Z. Current state: routing override in place, streaming disabled for affected customers, preproc scaled, canary shows p99 improved to ~1.6s. Hotfix ready to merge pending smoke tests. Next steps for oncall: watch p99/p95 for 1h, validate no customer errors, coordinate prod rollout of hotfix, after 2h revert routing override and re-enable streaming for customers.

frank: acknowledged. I'll take this and monitor 10:00-12:00Z. If anything changes I'll escalate. Thanks all.

alice: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will keep thread open until hotfix is in prod and we re-enable streaming. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident note auto-generated: incident_id INC-2025-082-17, severity: SEV3 (SLO breach), impacted: streaming-tail latency for json-mode; mitigations applied.

frank: quick handover summary (for the next oncall):
- root cause: sync full-schema validation in tokenizer (commit abc1234) causing CPU blocking in preproc
- current mitigations: routing override, streaming disabled for 3 customers, scaled preproc, canary streaming-fallback, schema-size guard
- next actions: monitor, roll hotfix to prod, validate, then revert routing & re-enable streaming, postmortem draft (bob + dave)

frank: I'll post updates to #incidents and #support if anything changes.

alice: thanks everyone. I'll add timeline to postmortem skeleton and ping product/legal if needed for customer comms.

carla: :+1: will keep canary running and share metrics in 15m.

bob: merging hotfix branch to main in 20m for canary deploy.

frank: thanks — taking over monitoring.
